text:
Kirill Kaprizov ended it 21 seconds into overtime, scoring on the power play to give Minnesota a 2-1 win in Montreal. Nick Suzuki had tied the game with just over a minute and a half left in regulation, and the Canadiens could not hold on after that. Kaprizov, drafted 135th overall in 2015, finished a play started by Matt Boldy and Quinn Hughes with a slap shot.

The Wild got there on the back of Jesper Wallstedt. Our numbers say the quality of chances Montreal created (expected goals) added up to 3.64 against him, and he gave up one. That is 2.64 goals saved above expected, meaning he stopped far more than a typical goalie would have. His best save came in the second period, when he stopped Alexandre Texier on a 30% chance. Wallstedt was a 20th overall pick in 2021, and he carried the Wild in a game they did not control.

MTL took 71 shot attempts to MIN's 55, won 36 of 55 faceoffs, and led the chance-quality count 3.64 to 2.91. Our simulation of every shot gave the Canadiens a 62% chance to win, so they deserved better. Bobby Brink's snap shot in the third period opened the scoring, and it was only a 26% chance. Jacob Fowler stopped 22 of 24 and was our second star. Minnesota takes a win it did not earn on play, and Montreal takes a loss it will likely look at as a missed chance. We have no streak or standings data to say more.
